newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco deal would require industry pay $368.5 billion.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco deal would require industry pay $368.5 billion.

text.p: A landmark tobacco agreement would require cigarette companies to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years to compensate the states and smokers, and to fund programs to help people quit smoking, states attorneys general said on Friday.

"Not one of these tobacco companies has yet paid a penny to anyone, but in this agreement, they agree to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years and who knows how much beyond that to individual claimants, state governments, tobacco control, public education and smoking cessation programs, and other vital causes," Connecticut Attorney General Dick Blumenthal said in a statement.

"They are subject to stiff penalties if they don't fully comply and meet goals. And they have to completely revamp their corporate culture. In exchange, they get no immunity, civil or criminal," Blumenthal said.

The deal also sets goals of reducing teen smoking by 42 pct in 5 years, 58 pct in 7 years and 67 pct in 10 years or cigarette companies would be penalized of up to $2 billion a year, according to the statement.
